literature_reality_check_summary: The post-.102 Reality Check section reports that LLM formalizers can fail on real CSPs even when solver-style answers agree, including excessive reasoning tokens and hard-coded solutions. SatIR reinforces that incomplete inputs need explicit UNKNOWN-preserving formal constraints, not forced labels. The orthographic constraint work shows deterministic hard constraints can expose architecture-specific failures hidden by aggregate answer agreement. Therefore Carnot must evaluate CSP formalization with solver-backed certificates, not answer agreement or parseability alone.
